fullPassage: "Let them eat cake." This phrase is often used to symbolize the gap between the rich and the poor. Though it is often reported that Marie Antoinette originally said it, this is actually a myth. The saying first appeared in an autobiography by Jean-Jacques Rousseau, which was written when Marie Antoinette was just nine years old and lived in Austria. Nobody knows why she became associated with the phrase, but, as a result, people today believe she was a cruel and thoughtless woman. However, historical documents show a much different side of Marie Antoinette. For instance, there is a letter she wrote to her family in Austria to describe an ongoing food shortage in France. In the letter, she wrote, "It is quite certain that in seeing the people who treat us so well despite their own misfortune, we are more obliged than ever to work hard for their happiness."
